 JUDGMENT
The Petitioner has filed this petition under Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by her in a road accident dated 25.05.2020.

2. The case of the Petitioner in brief is that, on 25.05.2020 at about 07.30 a.m., the petitioner was walking on the left side of the road near Arali Tree, Varthur lake SCCH-24 road, Bengaluru, at that time the driver of the Tata Ace bearing Reg.No.KA53D6328 came at high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against her, as a result, she fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately, she was rushed to Suraksha Multi Specialty Hospital, Bengaluru, for further treatment.
Prior to the accident, she was working as Senior Stylist in PB Associates, Bengaluru and was earning sum of Rs.32,600/ per month.
Due to the injuries sustained in the said accident, she is not able to continue her job and is under complete bed rest, as such loss of income and undergoing great mental agony and sufferings.
The Whitefiled Traffic Police have registered a case under Cr.No.74/2020 for the offences punishable u/Sec.279 and 337 of IPC against the driver of the Tata Ace bearing Reg.No.KA53D6328.
The 1st respondent being the RC owner and the 2nd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to her.
SCCH-24 3. In response to the summons, the Respondent No.2 has appeared through its counsel and filed written statement but the respondent no.1 has not appeared and hence placed exparte.

4. The Respondent No.1 in the written statement have denied the case of the petitioner as false,
admitted issuance of policy but their liability is subject to terms and conditions and submitted that there is non compliance of Sections 134(c) and 158(6) of M.V.Act.
Further submitted that the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective DL but even then entrusted by the respondent No.1 in contravention of policy conditions.

There was no negligence on the part of the driver of the insured vehicle but the accident occurred due to sole negligence of the petitioner but even then the insured vehicle has been implicated in collusion for wrongful gain, a false case has SCCH-24 been foisted against the insured vehicle in collusion.
Therefore, prayed for dismissal of the petition against them.
5. On the basis of the above pleadings the following issues are framed:

Smt.Anitha Raghunath vs Mr.Praveen Kumar on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24107962/
2
1. Whether the Petitioner proves that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving by driver of Tata ACE bearing Reg.No.KA53D6328 and in the said accident petitioner sustained injuries ?
2. Whether the Petitioner is entitled for Compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?

From whom?
3.
What order or award?

6. The Petitioner in order to prove her case, she has examined herself as PW.1 and got marked documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.14 and also examined Dr.Ramesh Orthopedic Surgeon at Victoria Hospital, as PW.2 and produced documents as per Exs.P.15 and P.16.
On the SCCH-24 other side the Respondent No.2 did not examine any witness nor produced any documents on their behalf.

7. Heard the arguments and perused the materials on record.
8.

On hearing both sides and perusal of the evidence on record this court answers the above issues as follows: Issue No.1: In the affirmative, Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative, Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following: REASONS 9.

Issue No.1: The Petitioner in order to prove that the accident was occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the TATA Ace bearing Reg.No.KA53MD6328 has examined herself as PW.1 and produced 8 documents as per Exs.P.1 to P.5, P7 to P.9.

She has specifically stated in her evidence that, on 25.05.2020 at about 07.30 a.m., she SCCH-24 was walking on the left side of the road near Arali Tree, Varthur lake road, Bengaluru, at that time the driver of the Tata Ace bearing Reg.No.KA53D6328 came at high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against her and caused the accident, as a result, she fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

On the other side, the Respondent No.2 has denied that the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle and specifically contended that there was negligence on the part of the petitioner herself.
In support of their defence the Respondent No.2 have not examined any witness nor produced any documents.
In the cross examination of the PW.1 nothing worth is elicited.

10. Further, the Petitioner apart from her oral evidence has produced the documents such as certified copies of FIR in Cr.No.0074/2020 of Whitefield Traffic Police Station, FIS, spot mahazar,
spot sketch, MVA report, notice u/sec.133 of MV Act, reply to the above notice and SCCH-24 chargesheet as per Exs.P.1 to P.5, P7 to P.9.
These all documents supports the case of the petitioner about the manner of accident.
The respondent No.2 has not lead any cogent evidence to prove negligence on the part of petitione and hence their defence is remained unproved.

Under these circumstances, relying upon the oral evidence of PW.1 coupled with the documents produced as per Exs.P.1 to P.5, P7 to P.9 and appreciating them which are public documents having presumptive value under law, in absence of contrary evidence this court is of the opinion that the driver of the offending vehicle driven it with rash or negligent manner and caused accident as alleged by the claimant.
Accordingly, issue No.1 is held in the affirmative.

Smt.Anitha Raghunath vs Mr.Praveen Kumar on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24107962/
3 11.
Issue No.2:

The Petitioner has further averred that, on account of accident, she not able to do computer typing work and she SCCH-24 is suffering from permanent disability and hence she is unable to do her earlier work/occupation.
The Petitioner in this regard has entered into witness box and deposed that due to the accidental injuries, she is suffering from permanent disability.
Apart from that, she has produced the wound certificate as per Ex.P.6.
As per Ex.P.6, the petitioner has sustained ulna Shaft 1/3rd right forearm.
Ex. P.12
/ Discharge card issued by Suraksha Multispeciality Hospital, wherein she was admitted as an inpatient from 25.05.2020 to 27.05.2020.
The petitioner has got examined Dr.Ramesh as PW.2.
This court while considering the Issue No.1 has already come to the conclusion that the accident occurred due to the rash or negligent driving of the driver of car.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation from the Respondents.

DISABILITY:-
12.
The PW.2 - Dr.Ramesh Orthopedic surgeon at Victoria Hospital, has produced clinical report and recent x SCCH-24 ray as per Exs.P.15 and P.6.

He has deposed that, as per oral statement by the patient xerox copy of discharge summary from Suraksha Multi Specialty Hospital, a female patient by name Smt.Anith Raghunath,
aged about 39 years old, gave history of RTA on 25.05.2020 and on examination, she had sustained oblique fracture right ulna and she took treatment Internal fixation of Ulna and he examined her recently on 12.12.2022 for disability assessment and she complained of pain right forearm difficulty to ablution lift weight over the head with right upper limb difficulty to do routine activities and on examination he found restriction of joint movement of right forearm pronation supination 35 dg normal 0.165 dg difficulty to ablution lift weight over the head with right upper limb power of right forearm 4/5 normal 5/5.

PW.2 further deposed that on radiological examination shows fracture united with implant in situ and the petitioner has got permanent disability of the right upper limb is at 26% SCCH-24 and to the whole body is 9%, which is permanent in nature and she needs one more surgery for removal of implants.

In the crossexamination of PW.2 it is brought out that he has not treated the petitioner, he have not seen the follow up records of the petitioner, the fracture is united, the petitioner is not using any support to use the limb, he has not seen the medical records of the petitioner with the same complaints which he deposed at para 5 of his chief examination affidavit and with difficulty the petitioner can do her daily activities.
Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, the period of treatment that she has undergone, her age, her functional disability is considered at 5% to the whole body.

Monthly income:
13.
The Petitioner has deposed in her evidence that, she was working as a senior Stylist in PB. Associates, Bengaluru and was earning sum of Rs.32,600/ per SCCH-24 month.
In this regard the petitioner has produced three salary slips with Sec.65B certificate at Ex.P11.

To support the said documents the petitioner has not Smt.Anitha Raghunath vs Mr.Praveen Kumar on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24107962/
4 examined her employer and hence mere production of salary slips without corroborating evidence cannot be considered in favour of the petitioner.

Therefore,
the version of the Petitioner that she was earning a sum of Rs.32.600/ per month and hence, the notional income needs to be considered.
At the time of accident the Petitioner was aged about 39 years as could be make out from Ex.P.10/Aadhar card of the petitioner wherein her birth year mentioned as1981.
The accident took place in the year 2020.

In absence of specific evidence for income, therefore by taking judicial notice of the notified notional income chart approved by the KSLSA the monthly notional income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.14,500/ per month.

As such,
Petitioner is entitled for the following compensation: SCCH-24 i) PAIN AND SUFFERING:
After the accident, the Petitioner was taken to Surakasha Multispeciality Hospital, wherein admitted as an inpatient on 25.05.2020 to 27.05.2020 for 3 days as per Exs.P.12/Discharge card.
Therefore, considering the nature of injuries and duration of treatment she has underwent, the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.45,000/ under this head.
ii) LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAID UP PERIOD:
As mentioned above the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the accident and was taken treatment in the above mentioned hospital.
Therefore, considering the nature of injuries and the duration of treatment it can be said that the Petitioner has required at least one month time for recovering from the injuries sustained by her.
SCCH-24
Hence, she is entitled for a sum of Rs.14,500/ under this head.
iii) MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The petitioner claimed that she incurred Rs.1,50,000/ towards medical expenses and produced 16 medical bills for Rs.84,018/ at Ex.P.13.
In the cross examination of PW.1 though suggestions are put that she got reimbursement of medical expenses but the said suggestions are denied by the petitioner.
No contrary evidence is lead by the respondent no.2.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.84,018/ under this head.
iv) LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME:
In so far as age of the Petitioner is concerned, the Aadhar card is produced as per Exs.P.10.
As per these document her age was 39 years as on the date of accident.
Therefore, as on the date of the accident the Petitioner's age SCCH-24 is considered as 39 years.
As per the dictum laid down in Sarala Verma's case the appropriate multiplier applicable to her age is 15.

Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled a sum of Rs.1,30,500/ (Rs.14,500/ x 12 x 15 x 5%=
Rs.1,30,500/) under this head.
(v) LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The Petitioner was aged about 39 years at the time of accident.

She has sustained grievous injuries and as per consideration of this Tribunal,
she is suffering from 5% permanent disability.
The Petitioner has to suffer this disability throughout her life.
Because of this she will have to lose some amenities and comforts.
Therefore, considering the age and nature of injuries that the Petitioner has suffered a sum of Rs.17,000/ is awarded under this head.

Smt.Anitha Raghunath vs Mr.Praveen Kumar on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24107962/
5 SCCH-24 vi) ATTENDANT, CONVEYANCE, FOOD AND NOURISHMENT
CHARGES:

After the accident, the Petitioner took treatment in Surakasha Multispeciality,
Hospital, wherein admitted as an inpatient for 3 days and underwent surgery.
Therefore, as during this period she must have spent considerable amount on her conveyance, attendant charges, food and nourishment etc.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled for a sum of Rs.17,000/ under this head.
vii) FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:
As per the version of the PW.2, the Petitioner is advised to undergo one more surgery for removal of implants.
But there is no estimation bill produced by the Petitioner or PW.2.

Therefore, looking to the earlier treatment cost and nature of injury and cross examination of PW.2, it appears it would be justifiable if an amount of Rs.10,000/ is awarded to the Petitioner under this head.
SCCH-24
Therefore the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.10,000/ under this head.

14. The Petitioner is entitled compensation under the following heads:
1. Pain & suffering Rs.45,000/
2.

Medical expenses Rs.84,018/
3. Loss of income during laid up Rs.14,500/ period 4.

Loss of future income Rs.1,30,500/
5. Loss of future amenities and Rs.17,000/ happiness 6. Attendant, conveyance, food and Rs.17,000/ nourishment charges
7. Future medical expenses Rs.10,000/ TOTAL Rs.3,18,018/
If it is rounded off it comes to Rs.3,18,100/ and therefore, the total compensation comes to Rs.3,18,100/ and same is awarded to the petitioner.
LIABILITY 15.
The Respondent No.2 has not proved its defence as discussed above.
Therefore, the Respondent Nos.1 and 2 are being the owner and the Insurer of the offending SCCH-24 vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.

However, as the Petitioner has proved the existence of insurance policy, the Respondent No.2 - insurer has got primary liability to compensate Smt.Anitha Raghunath vs Mr.Praveen Kumar on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/24107962/
6 the Petitioner.
The Petitioner has claimed for a sum of Rs.15,00,000/ but she is entitled only for a sum of Rs.3,18,100/ with interest @ 6% per annum.
Therefore, the petition needs to be allowed in part.
Accordingly Issue No.2 is held partly in the affirmative.
16. Issue No.3:
For the reasons and discussions made above and finding to the above issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following: ORDER The petition is hereby allowed in part with cost.
SCCH-24

The Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,18,100/ (Rupees Three lakhs Eighteen Thousand and One Hundred only)
from the Respondents along with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of depositing the amount.
The respondents 1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
However, the Respondent No.2 insurer is directed to deposit the compensation amount with interest within sixty days from the date of this Judgment.
On deposit of compensation and interest, entire amount shall be released in favour of the Petitioner by way of epayment on proper SCCH-24 identification and due acknowledgment as per rules.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw decree accordingly.
